title: Vegetable Dhansak
ingredients: ½ cup toor dal ((arhar dal or split pigeon peas))
¼ cup chana dal ((Bengal gram dal or split Indian chickpeas))
1 cup methi greens ((fresh fenugreek leaves, chopped. If using frozen use ½ cup. See ingredients list above for substitution))
¼ cup packed cilantro (+ 2 tablespoons more for garnish.)
2 tablespoons avocado oil or any neutral oil ((you can cut down to 1 tbsp but 2 really helps brown the onions nicely))
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
½ tsp caraway seeds ((shahi jeera, optional))
¼ tsp fenugreek seeds or methi seeds
method: Combine lentils, cauliflower, squash, methi, potatoes, tomatoes, ¼ cup coriander and garlic in a pressure cooker or pot.
Add water to cover (~3 cups in a cooker).
Cook until lentils and vegetables are soft (or simmer stovetop, stirring).
Toast whole spices for the blend (except turmeric, nutmeg, saffron) ~5 minutes; cool.
Stir in turmeric, nutmeg and saffron; grind to a fine powder.
Brown onions with salt and pepper in oil.
Add ginger-garlic paste briefly.
Add cooked lentils/veg with 3 cups water.
Blend partly smooth with an immersion blender, leaving some texture.
Bring to a boil; stir in dhansak masala and salt (optional tomato for colour).
Cover and cook 30–45 minutes, stirring, until glossy.
Garnish with remaining coriander; serve hot.

title: Cauliflower and Black Eyed Peas Curry (Low Carb + Vegan)
ingredients: 14 oz black eyed peas ((canned or homecooked or frozen are all fine))
8 oz cremini mushrooms or button mushrooms ((quartered))
½ head cauliflower ((separated into small florets))
1 cup cashew milk ((or coconut milk. You can make the cashew milk at home by blending ¼ cup raw cashews with ¾ cup water))
method: Blend tomatoes, onion and one mushroom smooth.
Sputter cumin in oil; add paste.
Cook until dark and dry; add cauliflower and remaining mushrooms.
Cover medium-low until nearly tender.
Add black-eyed peas with 2 cups cooking liquid or water.
Stir in coconut or cashew milk, salt and a little garam masala.
Garnish with coriander.

title: Vegan Low Carb Keto Chili
ingredients: 14 oz diced tomatoes (use the entire can, juices and all)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
method: Warm olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Soften onion, celery and garlic with salt and pepper about 5 minutes until translucent, not browned.
Crumble in the vegan mince and cook 5 minutes, stirring so it does not stick.
Stir through diced tomatoes with their juices and the tomato paste. Cook another 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down into the base.
Add chili powder, cumin, optional paprika and sage. Cook 5 minutes more, stirring often.
Pour in stock or water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 30 minutes. For a thicker chili, uncover for the last 10 minutes to reduce.
Finish with liquid aminos if using; adjust salt and pepper.
Serve hot with parsley if liked. Flavours deepen after a night in the fridge.

title: Vegan French Fry Casserole
ingredients: 1 teaspoon avocado oil or any neutral oil
2 teaspoons rosemary (or sage, Start with 1 tsp, taste, and add more if you want. If using fresh herbs use 1 to 2 tbsp instead.)
2 cups oat milk (or any nondairy milk, unsweetened)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
20 oz shoestring French fries (frozen, not thawed)
method: Heat the oven to 175°C / 350°F.
In a 30 cm / 12-inch cast-iron skillet, warm the oil. Soften garlic, onion, celery and carrot with salt and pepper until tender, not browned.
Stir in diced sweet potato; cover 3–5 minutes until nearly tender. Add bell pepper, rosemary or sage, and cumin; cook 2 minutes.
Crumble in vegan mince and cook until it begins to colour.
Sprinkle over the flour and stir until absorbed. Whisk in oat milk; bring just to a boil, then take off the heat. Season.
If the pan is not oven-safe, tip the filling into a baking dish.
Arrange frozen shoestring fries in one or two layers over the creamy filling so the bottom softens in the sauce and the top crisps.
Bake 1 hour. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Vegan Ros Omelette
ingredients: 1 medium shallot (or red onion, finely minced)
2 large shallots (Slice one and cut the other in a fine dice.)
2 dry Kashmiri red chili peppers (broken into pieces)
A small piece dagad phool (stoneflower, optional)
2 cups dried mushrooms (or use 8 oz fresh crimini or portobello mushrooms, chopped)
method: Xacuti gravy: soak dried mushrooms in 3 cups boiling water 30 minutes. Keep the liquid; chop mushrooms, trimming tough stems.
Toast cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, chilli pieces, peppercorns, coriander, cumin, fennel and optional stoneflower in 1 tsp oil until fragrant.
Add sliced shallot and poppy seeds; roast ~2 minutes until the onion colours. Cool.
Blend the toasted mix with tomatoes to a smooth paste.
Sauté diced shallot in 1 tsp oil until golden; cook ginger-garlic paste 1 minute.
Add mushrooms briefly, then the paste and mushroom soaking liquid (thin with water or stock if needed).
Simmer covered ~20 minutes until oil flecks the surface.
Stir in coconut milk; cook 5 minutes. Season and finish with cilantro.
Omelette: whisk chickpea flour, rice flour, turmeric, minced shallot, chilli, cilantro, cumin and salt.
Stream in water while whisking to a lump-free pourable batter.
Oil a hot skillet. Spread ~⅓ cup batter into a round.
Cook until the top sets and edges brown; flip 30 seconds; fold in half (and again if liked).
Ladle gravy into a bowl, nest the folded omelette in the centre and spoon more gravy over. Garnish with coriander.
Offer lemon wedges, chopped onion and soft rolls alongside.
notes: Tags: Ros Omelette. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: 1-Pot French Onion Soup (Vegan!)
ingredients: 2 Tbsp oil or vegan butter (or sub twice the amount in water, plus more as needed to prevent sticking)
2 medium yellow onions, peeled + sliced into slightly larger than 1/4-inch rounds
1 healthy pinch each salt and black pepper, plus more to taste
1 cup thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms (adds depth of flavor and a bit of texture // okay to omit)
1 Tbsp arrowroot starch or cornstarch (optional // or all purpose flour if not gluten-free)
1 ½ tsp fresh thyme leaves, lightly chopped (or sub 3/4 tsp dried thyme)
1 Tbsp coconut aminos (or sub half the amount with tamari as it’s saltier)
Croutons (gluten-free as needed // see notes for instructions)
method: Warm oil, vegan butter or a splash of water in a large pot. Add onions sliced a little thicker than ¼ inch; stir, cover.
Cook medium 3–4 minutes until just colouring, then lower the heat and cook 30–40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until golden and sweet (longer for deeper colour). Season lightly as they cook.
When nearly done, add garlic and shiitakes; cook 2–3 minutes. Stir in optional arrowroot until coated.
Add bay leaves, thyme, broth and coconut aminos (hold the miso).
Cover and simmer ~20 minutes; uncover 5–10 minutes to concentrate slightly.
Loosen miso with ~¼ cup warm broth until smooth; stir into the soup.
Taste; adjust salt, pepper, aminos or miso.
Ladle hot with croutons and extra herbs. Refrigerate 4–5 days or freeze up to 1 month; keep croutons separate.
notes: Tags: french onion soup, vegan french onion soup. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Caramelized Onion Tart With Olives
ingredients: 3 cups all purpose flour (can use 1/2 whole wheat and half all purpose)
3 yellow onions (about 1 ½ pounds, thinly sliced)
1/2 cup kalamata olives (pitted, then left whole or coarsely chopped)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
method: Dough: bloom yeast in 1 cup lukewarm water with sugar.
Mix in flour, salt and 1 tbsp oil; knead to a soft, pliable dough, adding water by the tablespoon if stiff.
Oil the dough; prove in a bowl ~1½ hours until risen.
Toss sliced garlic with 1 tbsp olive oil; set aside.
Onions: heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet. Soften onions 5 minutes, then salt and cook 15–20 minutes until deep golden, deglazing if they stick.
Heat the oven to 260°C / 500°F.
Halve the dough (freeze one half if wished). Roll or press one piece to about 28×20 cm.
Spread caramelised onions thinly over the base; scatter olives and garlic; brush edges with the garlic oil. Season lightly.
Bake ~14 minutes until the rim is golden and the tart lifts easily. Slice and serve hot.

title: Homemade Chili Powder
ingredients: 1 ounce dried mild red chiles, such as ancho, guajillo, or New Mexico
1 Tbsp cocoa powder (optional // Dutch processed for deeper flavor)
method: For whole dried chillies: stem, seed and discard the stems/seeds.
Toast chillies in a dry skillet 1–2 minutes per side until fragrant; cool.
Grind toasted chillies to a powder, then blend or shake with cumin, garlic powder, oregano, smoked paprika, coriander, optional cayenne, cinnamon and optional cocoa.
If starting with ground chilli: stir all spices together in a jar.
Use in chilli, tacos, soups and spice rubs.
Store airtight up to 6 months at room temperature, or chill/freeze up to 1 year.

title: Spaghetti Squash Pasta with Garlicky Alfredo Sauce

Blend cashews with garlic, nutritional yeast, salt and almond milk until silky. Adjust seasoning; blend in basil if using.

Toss with the sauce 1–2 minutes until hot and slightly thickened.
Serve at once with herbs, vegan parmesan or chilli flakes.

title: Instant Pot Spaghetti Squash (20 Minutes!)
method: Pick a squash that fits your Instant Pot (for 6-quart, under ~20 cm / 8 inches long; up to ~4 lb).
Halve lengthwise carefully with a sharp knife.
Scoop out seeds and stringy pulp.
Pour 1 cup water into the pot; set the trivet. Nest both halves cut-side up so they fit. Seal.
Pressure cook on high 8 minutes (allow 5–10 minutes to pressurise).
Quick-release; check that a fork pierces the flesh easily. Cook longer if needed.
Cool briefly; cancel, remove, flip flesh up and scrape into strands with a fork.
Serve with marinara, pesto or a white wine sauce. Refrigerate 3–4 days; not freezer-friendly.

title: 1-Pot Green Curry with Chickpeas, Kale, and Sweet Potato
ingredients: 1/4 cup water (or sub small amount of oil)
2/3 cup diced or thinly sliced shallot or onion
2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
2 Tbsp coconut aminos, (DIVIDED, plus more to taste (or sub sea salt to taste)
1/2 cup water or vegetable broth (vegetable broth will add more flavor, so go easy with additional salt)
1 15-oz can chickpeas, rinsed and drained (~1 ½ cups drained chickpeas, )
1 tsp maple syrup or coconut sugar (optional // omit for less sugar)
3 cups chopped kale or other sturdy green (such as collard greens)
method: In a large pot, soften shallot and ginger in water (or a little oil) 3–4 minutes.
Add garlic briefly, then green curry paste; cook 2 minutes.
Coat sweet potato with half the coconut aminos and curry powder 2–3 minutes. Pour in coconut milk and broth or water.
When simmering, add chickpeas; keep at a gentle simmer.
Cover 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potato is tender.
Taste the broth; balance with maple, more aminos, curry powder or paste.
Stir in kale; cover 2–3 minutes until wilted. Rest uncovered a minute.
Serve alone or over grains; top with cilantro, citrus and cashews.
Refrigerate 3–4 days or freeze 1 month; loosen with coconut milk when reheating.

title: Vegan Caesar Salad with BBQ Sweet Potato Croutons
ingredients: 1 batch BBQ Roasted Sweet Potato Croutons

1 cup shredded or thinly sliced carrots
1 ½ tsp spicy mustard (// either will work)
1 healthy pinch each sea salt + pepper (plus more to taste)
1 tsp olive oil (optional // omit if oil-free)
method: Prepare BBQ sweet potato croutons (or plain roasted sweet potato); set aside.
Whisk hummus with mustard, lemon zest and juice, chopped capers and brine, garlic, salt, pepper, maple and optional oil until creamy. Adjust seasoning.

title: Easy Banana Ice Cream (Tips + 10 flavors!)
ingredients: 2 ½ cups sliced frozen ripe banana

Berry (base recipe + 1 cup frozen mixed berries)

method: Peel ripe spotted bananas; slice 1 cm thick. Freeze flat on parchment until firm (3–4 hours or overnight).

For scoopable ice cream, freeze in a covered tub or parchment-lined loaf tin 2–3 hours; soften 15–30 minutes if rock-hard.
Best within a week; keeps covered up to 1 month frozen. Top with fruit, cacao nibs, nut butter or coconut if liked.

title: Bombay Potatoes

title: Perfect Vegan Cornbread
ingredients: 3/4 cup unsweetened plain almond milk (plus 1 Tbsp // adjust if altering batch size)
1 tsp lemon juice or apple cider vinegar
1/2 cup organic cane sugar or granulated sugar
3/4 cups fine yellow cornmeal (plus 1 Tbsp // adjust if altering batch size)
3/4 cups unbleached all-purpose flour* (plus 1 Tbsp // adjust if altering batch size)
method: Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F; grease an 20 cm / 8-inch square tin.
Make flax egg; rest. Curdle almond milk with lemon; stir in baking soda.
Whisk melted vegan butter with sugar; whisk in applesauce and flax, then the milk mixture.
Fold in salt, cornmeal and flour until just combined (thin and slightly lumpy is fine).
Bake 28–37 minutes until edges are golden and a tester comes out clean.
Rest a few minutes; serve with vegan butter and maple if liked.
Airtight a couple of days, or freeze longer.

method: Process shredded coconut until it clumps like dough when squeezed (~45–60 seconds, then short pulses).
Add maple, peppermint and 1 tsp melted coconut oil; process until it holds when pressed.
Shape ~1-tbsp discs; freeze on parchment 10 minutes (~14 patties).

Dip chilled discs on a fork; drain excess; return to parchment.
Chill 8–10 minutes until set. Serve cool or room temperature.
Room temp 4–5 days, fridge 2 weeks, freezer 1 month.

title: Garlic & Herb Sweet Potato Nourish Bowl (30 Minutes!)
ingredients: 1/3 cup chopped red bell pepper or cherry tomatoes
1 healthy pinch each sea salt and black pepper
1 Tbsp dulse (or other sea vegetable or sprout of choice // optional)
method: Heat oven to 200°C / 400°F. Rub halved sweet potato with oil; bake on parchment ~25 minutes until tender (quarter large ones).
Toss parsley, pepper or tomatoes, onion, lemon, salt and pepper for the herb salad.
Stir hummus with lemon, dill and garlic for the sauce; adjust seasoning or dilute with more hummus.
Assemble romaine with parsley salad, sweet potato, hummus, sauerkraut, tahini and za’atar. Optional lemon, dulse and chilli sauce; serve with dill garlic sauce.
Store components separately: potato 2–3 days, greens 3–4, sauce 4–5. Reheat potato until hot.

title: 'Whatever Floats Your Boat' Raw Cacao Energy Bars
ingredients: ½ cup dates, pitted and soaked in water
¼ cup raw dark chocolate chips (optional, for drizzle)
method: Pulse cashews and pumpkin seeds until finely chopped; tip into a bowl with cacao powder and nibs.
Process soaked dates and apricots with 2 tbsp water to a paste.
Mix fruit paste into the nut mix until sticky and slightly crumbly.
Press firmly into a parchment-lined loaf tin; press almonds on top.
Chill 2–3 hours. Optional dark chocolate drizzle. Cut into 5 bars.
notes: Raw / no-bake. Fruit binds the bars, so liquid sweeteners are not a 1:1 swap. Credit: Megan Olson / PaleoHacks. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Ethiopian Lentil Stew Recipe
ingredients: 1 cup red lentils (soaked for up to an hour. Drain out all water before use).)
1 heaping tbsp ginger garlic paste (you can also crush 6 cloves garlic with a 1-inch knob of ginger into a paste)
method: Dry-sauté diced onion with a teaspoon of salt over medium heat until soft and beginning to brown.
Stir in 1 tbsp vegan niter kibbeh and ginger-garlic paste; cook a couple of minutes.
Add tomatoes; cook until soft and pulpy.
Stir in berbere, coriander and cumin; cook with the base a couple of minutes.
Add drained lentils and 2 cups water. Boil, cover and simmer 20–25 minutes until very soft and thick, adding water or lowering heat as needed.
Finish with the remaining tablespoon of niter kibbeh and salt. Serve when thick, bubbling and flecked with oil.
notes: Tags: ethiopian lentil stew, ethiopian lentil stew recipe, lentil stew recipe. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Vegan Shakshuka
ingredients: 1/3 cup fresh parsley (chopped + more to sprinkle on top)
1/8 teaspoon chili powder (+ more to taste)
1/2 teaspoon paprika powder (+ more to taste)
method: Soft-fry sliced onions in olive oil. Add garlic, bell pepper and parsley.
Add ¼ cup water; cook until the pepper softens.
Stir in tomatoes, salt, cumin, chilli and paprika; simmer and adjust spices.
Whisk chickpea flour with kala namak and enough water for a thick pourable batter.
Spoon dollops of batter onto the sauce; cover until the “eggs” set.
Finish with parsley; serve with toast.

title: Vegan burrito with chipotle tempeh
ingredients: 60 ml / ¼ cup mild olive oil, divided
400 g / 14 oz can of chopped tomatoes
30 ml / 2 tbsp mild olive oil, divided
2 x 400 g / 14 oz cans of black beans
8 x 25 cm / 10" flour tortillas (GF if required)
200 g / 1 cup long grain rice, cooked
method: Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F; line a tray.
Pulse tempeh to a coarse mince. Toss with 2 tbsp oil; bake ~30 minutes, stirring halfway.
Soft-fry onion in remaining 2 tbsp oil; add garlic until translucent.
Bloom cumin, smoked paprika and salt 1 minute. Stir in chipotle paste loosened with water; cook briefly.
Add tomatoes, salt and a can of water. Simmer until thick; balance with salt, pepper, sugar and lime. Fold in baked tempeh.
Beans: sauté white/light-green spring onion in 2 tbsp oil; add garlic. Season with spices and salt.
Add drained beans and a splash of water; mash some for texture. Cook dry; finish with lime and salt.
Pico: mix diced cherry tomatoes, spring onion and cilantro; season with lime, salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar.
Warm tortillas until pliable. Fill with rice, beans, tempeh, pico and avocado; fold and roll tightly.
Toast seam-side down on a hot griddle; serve with hot sauce.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Roasted vegetable pasta
ingredients: 2 tsp roasted vegetable spice mix (any brand)
A large handful of basil and/or parsley leaves
100 g / 3.5 oz vegan feta or other similar cheese, to serve (optional)
method: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Cut aubergine into quarters and courgette into half-moons (~1.25 cm thick); chunk the pepper.
Toss with 2 tbsp oil, oregano, roast spice mix, salt and pepper. Roast 25 minutes, stirring once.
Halve cherry tomatoes; toss with 1 tbsp oil, oregano, grated garlic, sugar and balsamic. Add to the tray; roast 10–15 minutes more.
Toss vegetables through cooked pasta (and optional chickpeas). Finish with herbs and crumbled vegan feta.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Mango granita
ingredients: 850 g / 30 oz can sweetened mango pulp
method: Stir mango pulp with ~4 tbsp lime juice until smooth.
Freeze in a shallow covered container 1 hour.
Scrape with a fork every hour until fluffy crystals form.
Spoon into chilled glasses; top with coconut yoghurt and lime zest.

title: Spring minestrone
ingredients: 200 g / 7 oz green asparagus (or more green beans)
100 g / 3.5 oz green beans (or more asparagus)
120 g / 1 cup frozen broad beans (or more green peas)
130 g / 1 cup frozen petite pois or green peas
200 g / 7 oz orzo or other small pasta (or add canned beans)
Lemon juice, to taste + zest for serving
25 g / 0.85 oz (a handful) roasted pistachios or other nuts
Extra virgin olive oil, approx 4 tbsp / 60 ml
method: Gentle-fry onion and leek in olive oil until translucent and bright.
Add garlic, carrot, fennel and salt; cook 5–10 minutes.
Dissolve stock cube in 250 ml water.
Prep courgette half-moons, potato coins and 1.25 cm asparagus/bean pieces. If using frozen broad beans, simmer 6 minutes, ice-shock and peel.
Add stock plus 2 litres water, pasta and potatoes. After 6 minutes add courgette; after 2 more minutes add asparagus, green beans and peas (cook pasta separately if making leftovers).
Loosen miso with water; stir in at the end. Season with salt, pepper and lemon.
Pesto: pound garlic with coarse salt; work in basil, then pistachios. Stir in nutritional yeast, lemon and enough oil to a thick paste; season.
Ladle soup; top with pesto and lemon zest.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy,Italian. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Yellow curry with tempeh
ingredients: 4 birds eye chillies, more if you like more heat
2 x 400 g / 14 oz cans of full fat coconut milk
Vegan fish sauce or soy sauce (or tamari if gluten-free)
20 ml / 1½ tbsp soy sauce or tamari (if gluten-free)
method: Process shallot, garlic, lemongrass, ginger, chillies and a pinch of salt (optional oil) to a fine paste.
Fry the paste in oil low–medium 5–10 minutes until opaque and fragrant.
Bloom turmeric and curry powder 1 minute. Add coconut milk, ~1 tbsp tamarind and optional 240 ml water.
Simmer ~10 minutes. Season with sugar, vegan fish sauce or soy (~1½ tbsp) and lime.
Marinate tempeh slices in soy 10 minutes. Pan-fry until golden or bake at 200°C / 390°F ~30 minutes.
Blanch broccoli ~3 minutes and mangetout 30–60 seconds in salted water.
Serve sauce over rice with tempeh and greens; finish with coriander.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Quick noodles with tempeh
ingredients: 15 ml / 1 tbsp chilli crisp / chilli oil
Approx. 2 tbsp / 30 ml high smoke oil
method: Toss bite-size tempeh with 1 tbsp soy; set aside.
Prep broccoli pieces and thick spring-onion segments (reserve dark greens).
Whisk remaining soy, maple, rice vinegar and chilli oil for the sauce.
Cook noodles 30 seconds under packet time; drain.
Sear tempeh in a hot wok with oil until golden both sides; remove.
Wipe wok; stir-fry broccoli until charred in spots, adding spring onion halfway. Season with a little soy; remove.
Toss noodles in the sauce in the hot wok.
Return veg and tempeh to heat through. Serve with chilli oil and green onion tops.
notes: Tags: Asian-inspired,comfort food,easy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan gyoza with tempeh
ingredients: 250 g / 8.8 oz oz chestnut / cremini mushrooms
2-3 tsp grated ginger, adjust to taste
15 ml / 1 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari), more to serve
method: Pulse mushrooms, then tempeh, to a coarse mince (do not paste).
Optional: stir-fry tempeh in oil until dry and browned; remove.
Soft-fry white/light spring onion in 2 tbsp oil; add garlic and ginger until fragrant.
Cook mushrooms until dark and dry. Stir in tempeh and chopped kimchi; season with soy to taste. Cool completely.
Fill wrappers with ~1½ tsp filling; wet edges and seal.
Pan-fry ~10 dumplings in 1 tsp oil 2–3 minutes until bottoms brown.
Add ~150 ml water; cover and steam ~10 minutes. Uncover; add oil and crisp bases 2–3 minutes.
Serve with soy mixed with chilli oil. Keep finished batches warm at 100°C / 210°F if needed.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Harissa carrots on pistachio cream
ingredients: Parsley or mint, to serve (or carrot tops)
Arils from ¼ pomegranate, to serve
160 g / 1¼ cup shelled pistachios, ideally peeled
Zest 1 small lemon + approx. 30 ml / 2 tbsp juice
60 ml / ¼ cup mild olive oil
method: Heat oven to 210°C / 410°F (fan 190°C / 375°F).
Trim carrots to even thickness; keep young ones unpeeled.
Oil and foil a head of garlic; roast ~30 minutes with the carrots.
Toss carrots in most of a mix of harissa, oil and maple; season well. Roast 15 minutes; brush with remaining marinade; roast 10–15 minutes more until tender. Optional brief broil for char.
Optional: blanch 130 g pistachios 2 minutes, ice-bath and peel (or soak in boiling water 10 minutes).
Blend peeled pistachios with oil, a few roasted garlic cloves, lemon zest, ~120 ml water and lemon juice to taste (~160 ml total liquid besides oil). Season.
Spread cream on a platter; top with carrots, pomegranate, chopped pistachios and herbs or carrot tops.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,Thanksgiving,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan pasta bake with blender bechamel
ingredients: 15 g / 0.5 oz dry porcini or 1 mushroom stock cube
150 g / 5.3 oz pressed smoked tofu* (see NOTES)
Herbs: 1 tsp rosemary, 1 tsp rubbed sage
15 ml / 1 tbsp all purpose soy sauce (or tamari)
400 g / 14 oz can peeled plum tomatoes*, crushed
160 g / 1¼ cup cashews, soaked in boiling water for 20 minutes
Small garlic clove or ½ tsp garlic powder
40 g / scant ½ cup coarse breadcrumbs
method: Steep porcini (or dissolve mushroom cube) in 300 ml boiling water. Soak cashews in boiling water 20 minutes.
Pulse mushrooms to a mince. Soft-fry onion in oil; add garlic, then mushrooms and herbs until dry.
Crush tomatoes. Pulse tofu fine.
Add tomatoes, tofu, soy, tomato paste, miso, bay, pepper, wine and strained mushroom stock (mince rinsed porcini into the sauce). Simmer ~25 minutes.
Parboil pasta 7 minutes less than packet; drain. Fold into the loose sauce; season.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F. Blend drained cashews with garlic, nutritional yeast, optional nutmeg, cornstarch, salt, pepper and 300 ml water until silky.
Rub oil into breadcrumbs; season (optional rosemary).
Spread pasta in a dish; pour béchamel over; top with crumbs. Bake ~30 minutes until set and golden.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,tofu,winter. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Lemon tofu
ingredients: 600 g / 21 oz of extra firm tofu*, pressed
Zest of 2 lemons and 120 ml / ½ cup lemon juice
method: Press extra-firm tofu well.
Whisk lemon zest and juice, salt, garlic powder, oregano, pepper, nutritional yeast and oil.
Cut tofu into even pieces; coat in marinade in a shallow dish; pour remaining marinade over.
Marinate at least 1 hour, flipping occasionally.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F (fan 180°C). Arrange on parchment (or dust with cornstarch and pan-fry until golden).
Bake until golden, flipping halfway (~30 minutes for cubes; 35–40 for larger pieces).

title: Tahini pasta with Brussels sprouts
ingredients: Zest ½ small lemon + 15 ml / 1 tbsp juice
Handful of roasted hazelnuts, to finish
method: Halve Brussels sprouts lengthwise; pan-fry in oil until soft and charred in places. Season.
Cook pasta 1 minute underdone; reserve 240 ml pasta water; drain.
Whisk tahini, miso, nutritional yeast, lemon zest/juice and maple; thin with a splash of pasta water.
Soft-fry garlic in a little oil until fragrant. Whisk in the tahini sauce, thinning as needed.
Toss pasta in the sauce; warm through sprouts. Adjust seasoning.
Plate with hazelnuts and optional vegan bacon.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Vegan nut roast
ingredients: 1 can of green lentils (or 250 g / 8.8 oz of cooked)
1 tbsp each, chopped rosemary, sage and thyme
300 g / 10.5 oz chestnut mushrooms, finely chopped
18 g / 2 tbsp psyllium husk powder (or 3 tbsp psyllium husks)
method: Toast nuts at 175°C / 345°F 8–10 minutes; cool. Rub skins from hazelnuts; chop larger nuts.
Raise oven to 210°C / 410°F. Toss diced celeriac with 1 tbsp oil, salt and smoked paprika; roast 30 minutes, flipping once.
Soft-fry shallot in 2 tbsp oil; add garlic and herbs until fragrant.
Dry-fry mushrooms in batches until browned and moisture evaporates; season.
Loosen miso with 4 tbsp water and balsamic.
Combine celeriac, nuts, shallot-mushroom mix, lentils, cranberries, breadcrumbs and psyllium; stir in miso mix. Rest 30 minutes.
Pack into a well-greased 2 lb tin; bake 60 minutes at 210°C, covering with foil after 30 minutes.
Rest before slicing with a serrated knife; serve with gravy.
notes: Tags: gluten-free,healthy,Thanksgiving,winter,Xmas. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Creamy polenta with balsamic mushrooms
ingredients: A chunk of vegan butter, optional
400 g / 14 oz chestnut mushrooms, cut into 7 mm / 0.25" slices
60 ml / ¼ cup quality balsamic vinegar
30 ml / 2 tbsp soy sauce or tamari (if GF)
A few springs of fresh thyme or ½ tsp dry thyme
method: Heat oven to 220°C / 425°F (fan 200°C / 390°F).
Whisk oil, balsamic, maple, grated garlic, thyme, smoked paprika and soy for the marinade.
Roast sliced mushrooms 10–15 minutes until juices mostly evaporate. Optional: roast a foil-wrapped oiled garlic head ~25 minutes alongside.
Toss mushrooms with marinade; roast 10 minutes more, stirring once, until glazed with thickened sauce.
Bring 1.2 litres water to a simmer (blend roasted garlic into some of the water first if using).
Stream in polenta mixed with salt while whisking; stir with a spoon as it thickens.
Cover on very low heat 5–10 minutes; rest covered 5 minutes. Stir in vegan butter, nutritional yeast and salt.
Loosen with liquid if needed. Serve topped with balsamic mushrooms and juices.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,winter. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Aubergine bake with cashew bechamel
ingredients: 45 ml / 3 tbsp olive oil, more if liked
3 x 400 g / 14 oz cans peeled plum tomatoes
A good pinch of chilli flakes (optional)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
method: Soak cashews in boiling water ≥30 minutes.
Heat oven to 220°C / 430°F (fan 200°C). Slice aubergine into 0.75 cm rounds; roast on parchment 25–30 minutes, flipping once, until lightly browned.
Toss minced olives with breadcrumbs, salt and 1–2 tbsp oil for the crumb.
Soft-fry onion in 2 tbsp oil; add garlic until fragrant.
Mash in tomatoes with cinnamon, oregano, cloves, optional chilli, salt and pepper. Simmer ~40 minutes until thick, adding water if dry. Balance with date nectar or sugar if acidic.
Blend drained cashews with 240 ml water or plant milk, garlic, nutritional yeast, cornstarch, optional lemon and nutmeg, salt and pepper until silky.
Heat oven to 200°C / 390°F (fan 180°C). Layer tomato sauce, aubergine, half the béchamel, more aubergine and sauce; finish with remaining béchamel and olive crumb.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest ≥30 minutes. Fridge 5 days or freeze portions.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Vegan bolognese (easy, protein-rich)
ingredients: 1-2 tbsp / 15-30 ml olive oil OR veggie stock (if oil-free)
100 g / 3.5 oz walnuts or sunflower seeds
1 tsp (more if using plain tofu) smoked paprika
15 ml / 1 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari if GF)
5 ml / 1 tsp brown sugar or date syrup (optional)
method: Soft-fry onion in 1 tbsp oil until translucent; add garlic until fragrant.
Pulse or finely dice mushrooms; cook with salt until dark and dry. Optional second tbsp oil; stir in smoked paprika, soy and Italian herbs.
Add passata and crumbled smoked tofu; season. Simmer ~30 minutes until very thick, stirring often.
Toast or leave raw walnuts; chop to small bits (not flour). Fold into the sauce.
Finish with balsamic, optional sugar and nutmeg; adjust salt and pepper.
Toss with cooked pasta, loosening with pasta water or olive oil. Better after overnight rest. Garnish with parsley and vegan parmesan.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,gluten-free,healthy,oil-free,tofu. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Healthy carrot muffins
ingredients: 100-150 g / ½-¾ cup sugar , coconut sugar for healthier option
180 g / 1½ cups wholemeal flour (or a reliable GF flour mix)
SPICES: 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp ginger, ½ tsp cardamom
½ tsp xanthan gum (only if using GF flour mix)
50 g / 1/3 cup cup chopped walnuts, pecans or pumpkin seeds
30 g / 2 tbsp finely chopped candied/glace ginger
method: Heat oven to 180°C / 355°F (fan 160°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Grate peeled carrots; use 250 g in a large bowl.
Mix with yoghurt, sugar (less for subtler sweetness), candied ginger, raisins and 80 ml water.
Fold in coconut and a third of the flour; then remaining flour in two additions with baking soda, baking powder, salt, spices and optional xanthan. Fold in nuts or seeds.
Divide among liners; optional coconut on top. Bake ~25 minutes until a skewer is clean. Cool completely.
Store airtight 3–4 days.
notes: Tags: comfort food,easy,oil-free,refined sugar-free. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Italian fennel salad
ingredients: 30 ml / 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
5 ml / 1 tsp maple syrup or brown sugar (optional)
method: Optional: toast walnuts dry or at 160°C / 320°F ~10 minutes; cool and chop.
Thinly slice fennel and red pepper; cut into bite-size pieces.
Slice celery, stripping tough strings. Rough-chop leaves; slice olives; chop optional artichokes.
Whisk balsamic, oil, optional maple, grated garlic, salt and pepper.
Toss salad ingredients (except nuts) with dressing; plate and top with walnuts. Serve at once.
notes: Tags: easy,gluten-free,healthy. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Ania (Lazy Cat Kitchen)

title: Easy Vegan Pesto (5 Minutes!)
ingredients: 2 cups packed fresh basil (large stems removed)
3 Tbsp pine nuts or walnuts (if nut-free, try sunflower seeds!)
1/4 tsp sea salt (plus more to taste)
method: Process basil, nuts, garlic, lemon, nutritional yeast and salt to a loose paste.
Stream in olive oil, then water a tablespoon at a time, to a thick pourable sauce (or use broth/water only for oil-free).
Adjust cheeseiness, salt, nuts, garlic or lemon. Use on noodles, bread or sauces.
Fridge up to 1 week; freeze in cubes up to 1 month.
notes: Tags: vegan pesto | Notes *I rely on a mix of extra virgin olive oil and water to make this pesto a “sauce.” If you’re trying to avoid oil, feel free to sub the EVOO for vegetable broth or water! *Nutrition information is a rough estimate calculated with lesser amount of nutritional yeast. *Recipe adapted from my Smashed Potatoes with Garlic Pesto . *Recipe as originally written makes ~1 cup pesto. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Dana Shultz (Minimalist Baker)

title: Strawberry Cheesecake Bars (Vegan + GF)
ingredients: 1 cup rolled oats (gluten-free certified as needed)
4 heaping cups super ripe strawberries, hulled and quartered ( (1 ½ lbs yields 4 heaping cups)
method: Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F; line an 20 cm / 8-inch square tin with parchment.
Blend oats, almonds and salt to a fine meal. Stir with maple and melted coconut oil until it holds when squeezed; press into the tin.
Bake crust 20–25 minutes until corners colour and the centre feels dry.
Blend strawberries with maple and starch; cook in a saucepan 20–25 minutes, stirring, until thick and reduced to ~1½ cups. Cool slightly.
Blend cashews, coconut cream, lemon, starch, salt, maple and optional vanilla until silky.
Spread ~1 cup strawberry purée over the crust; pour on cheesecake batter; reserve remaining purée for topping if liked.
Bake 45–55 minutes until edges colour and the centre just jiggles. Chill covered 6–8 hours or overnight.
Lift out; cut into 16 squares. Fridge 3–4 days or freeze 1 month.
notes: Tags: gluten free strawberry cheesecake, strawberry cheesecake, strawberry cheesecake bars, vegan strawberry cheesecake | Notes *Prep time includes cooling cheesecake bars for 6 hours. *Nutrition information is a rough estimate calculated with the lesser amount of coconut oil and without optional ingredients. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Dana Shultz (Minimalist Baker)

title: The BEST Vegan Grilled Cheese Sandwich
ingredients: 2 large slices vegan bread of your choice
1 Tbsp vegan butter (// use more or less depending on size of bread)
4-5 Tbsp Vegan Cheddar Cheese (spread // or sub comparable amount of store-bought cheddar cheese slices or shreds)
method: Warm a cast-iron or non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Butter both sides of the bread.
Lightly toast both sides in the pan 1–2 minutes; remove.
Spread vegan cheddar on the inner faces; sandwich together.
Return to the pan; cook, flipping, 5–8 minutes until deep golden and the cheese melts (lower heat if browning too fast).
Serve hot, sliced if liked.
notes: Tags: vegan grilled cheese | Notes *Nutrition information is a rough estimate calculated with sourdough bread. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Dana Shultz (Minimalist Baker)

title: Quinoa Chickpea Salad
ingredients: 3 cups cooked quinoa (from 1 cup dried quinoa)
3 cups cooked chickpeas (from two 14.5 oz cans or cooked from 1 cup dried chickpeas. Be sure to drain out any liquid or brine.)
2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar (you can use more vinegar if you like a tart dressing. I don't like mine too acidic)
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
2 tablespoons maple syrup (can use stevia or any other sweetener)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
method: Whisk apple cider vinegar and olive oil until emulsified; whisk in maple, garam masala, cumin, salt and pepper.
Combine quinoa, chickpeas, pepper, onion, cucumber, carrot, celery, kale, herbs, pumpkin seeds and raisins.
Toss with the vinaigrette. Serve cool or room temperature.
notes: Tags: chickpea quinoa salad, quinoa salad recipe. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Vegan Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
ingredients: 3 cup cooked basmati rice (from 1 cup raw rice)
1 tbsp sesame oil (or any neutral oil)
method: Mix cooked rice with vegan yoghurt and salt.
Heat sesame oil; sputter mustard seeds. Add hing, curry leaves and dry chillies briefly.
Stir in ginger, peanuts, cashews, optional fenugreek and urad dal. Toast medium-low until dal and peanuts are light gold.
Pour tempering over the rice; mix. Adjust salt and serve.
notes: Tags: Curd Rice, thayir sadam, vegan curd rice | Vegan yogurt cost estimate is based on the cost of making my homemade vegan yogurt recipe . Using store-bought yogurt will increase the estimated cost. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Chunky Pinto Bean Soup
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper to taste
14 oz extra firm tofu (water pressed out, cut into four slabs)
1 large bell pepper (any color, finely chopped)
28 oz cooked or canned pinto beans (from two 14-oz cans or cooked from 1 cup dried pinto beans. Strain out all liquid.)
8 oz cremini mushrooms or button mushrooms (sliced)
4-5 cups mushroom stock (or vegetable stock or water)
method: Crumble tempeh into a small dish; rub with sage, oregano, salt, pepper and 1 tsp oil. Bake at 175°C / 350°F 20 minutes.
Mix flour with sage, oregano, salt and pepper. Dredge tofu slabs; brown in 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven on all sides. Cool; cube 1 cm. Reserve leftover flour.
In the same pot, soften onion, carrot, celery and bell pepper with salt and pepper ~5 minutes.
Add garlic and jalapeño 1 minute; stir in bay, sage and oregano.
Stir in remaining flour. Deglaze with optional wine until evaporated.
Add pinto beans, baked tempeh, tofu cubes and mushrooms with 3 cups stock (add more for a soupier pot).
Boil; simmer medium-low 10 minutes. Stir in soy and Cajun seasoning; return to a boil. Fold in scallions.
Serve hot or warm.
notes: Tags: chunky soup, pinto bean soup, pinto bean soup recipe. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Dal Palak (Indian Spinach Dal)
ingredients: ½ cup toor dal (also called arhar dal, toor dal or split pigeon peas)
½ cup moong dal (split yellow mung beans)
1 tsp oil (use avocado or any neutral oil, or refined coconut oil, which is flavorless)
½ tsp red pepper flakes (or 1 dried red chili pepper. Tweak the amount to your preference for heat.)
1 medium onion (red onion preferred, finely chopped)
2 tomatoes (pureed, or ¾ cup canned puree)
½ tsp cayenne (optional if sensitive to heat)
1 tbsp oil (avocado or any neutral oil, or unrefined coconut oil)
12-14 cloves garlic (thinly sliced. You can use more or less, but the more garlicky this dal is, the tastier it gets.)
method: Wash toor and moong dals; cover with water by 5 cm and add ¼ tsp turmeric. Pressure-cook ~3 whistles, or simmer covered ~30 minutes until very soft; whisk smooth. (Cook ahead and fridge up to 4 days.)
Sputter ½ tsp mustard seeds in 1 tsp oil; lower heat and add chilli flakes and hing.
Soft-fry onion with salt 3–5 minutes. Cook ginger-garlic paste 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, coriander, remaining turmeric and optional cayenne; cook until dry.
Wilt in spinach; stir in the whisked dal. Thin with up to 2 cups water; boil then simmer 5 minutes. Salt and lemon to taste.
Second tadka: heat 1 tbsp oil; bloom mustard, cumin and sliced garlic until golden (not bitter). Off heat, add optional paprika.
Pour over the dal; serve hot.
notes: Tags: dal palak, Garlicky spinach dal, palak dal | Add a little more oil to the garlic tadka if the garlic begins to stick. Stay with the tadka - don't walk away - because the garlic can brown fast. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Mushroom Biryani
ingredients: ½ tsp caraway seeds (shahi jeera. Use cumin seeds as a substitute)
2 tablespoons avocado oil or any neutral oil
1 heaping tbsp ginger garlic paste (or crush together six cloves garlic and an inch-long knob of ginger)
2 tomatoes (pureed. Or use 1 cup canned tomato puree)
1 tsp cayenne (or paprika, which will add more color and less heat. You can use Kashmiri chilli powder if you have it)
12 oz cremini mushrooms (or button mushrooms, sliced.)
method: Boil soaked basmati with 6 cups water, caraway, cardamom, cloves, bay and salt. Cook uncovered 6–7 minutes until just tender with a slight bite; drain at once.
Bloom bay, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon in oil 1 minute. Caramelise sliced onion with salt and caraway; cook ginger-garlic paste 1 minute.
Stir in 2 tbsp cilantro and tomato puree, then coriander, cumin, cayenne and turmeric. Cook until dry; add cashews and mushrooms.
Add 1 cup stock or water; boil and simmer 5 minutes. Season.
Low heat: layer rice over the mushroom sauce. Top with remaining cilantro and fried onions. Cover tightly; steam 5 minutes. Rest 10 minutes without lifting the lid.
Scoop to the bottom so each plate gets sauce and rice.
notes: Tags: comfort food, Mushroom Biryani, One Pot, quick, spicy | Salt the water you cook the rice in, just as you would salt pasta water. The rice will soak in the flavors of the salt and the spices as it cooks. If sensitive to heat, make sure you know how spicy the garam masala or biryani masala you are using is. If you want less heat, skip the cayenne or add less of it. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Vegan Irish Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 6 oz cremini mushrooms or button mushrooms (minced)
1 tbsp thyme (chopped. If using dry thyme use 1 tsp)
2 tbsp mint (chopped. If using dry mint use 1 to 2 tsp)
28 oz brown lentils (canned or cooked, drained)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
method: Soft-fry garlic briefly, then onion with salt and pepper. Add carrot, celery and bell pepper.
Stir in mushrooms; cook with optional whiskey until mostly dry. Add crumbled tempeh.
Mix in tomato paste, mustard, tamari, paprika, optional cayenne, mint and thyme.
Fold in lentils and peas; warm through. Season; set aside.
Mash cooked potatoes with salt, pepper, rosemary, oil and plant milk until fluffy.
Oil a baking dish; spread filling; top with even mash. Fork a pattern on top.
Bake at 205°C / 400°F 25–30 minutes until the edges brown and crisp. Rest 10 minutes.
notes: Tags: Vegan Irish Shepherd's Pie, vegan shepherd's pie, vegan shepherd's pie recipe. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Tofu Dal Tadka
ingredients: ½ cup toor dal (yellow split peas or pigeon peas)
½ tsp cayenne (or paprika for less heat)
16 oz high protein tofu (or extra firm tofu with water pressed out. Cut the tofu in ½-inch cubes)
method: Cook masoor and toor with water and turmeric until very soft (pressure ~3 whistles, Instant Pot ~10 minutes, or stovetop 20–30 minutes). Whisk creamy.
Brown onion in 1 tsp oil with a pinch of salt. Soften tomatoes with ginger-garlic and cilantro until pulpy.
Bloom coriander, cumin, cayenne/paprika and 1 tsp garam masala ~30 seconds.
Stir in dal (thick but pourable). Cover; simmer medium-low then low ~10 minutes. Salt.
Tadka: sputter mustard and hing in 2 tbsp oil; add cayenne/paprika, garlic and ½ tsp garam masala. Fry tofu cubes until lightly crusted.
Pour tadka and tofu into the dal; simmer 5 minutes. Serve hot.
notes: Tags: tofu dal tadka, vegan anda dal | If the dal is too thick for your liking, feel free to add more water. Always check if you need more salt after adding water. The dal will thicken upon standing. When you reheat, add more water if needed. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Caribbean Black Eyed Peas Stew Recipe
ingredients: 2 small bell peppers (any color is fine, diced)
method: Cook garlic briefly in coconut oil. Soft-fry onion with salt and pepper ~5 minutes until beginning to brown.
Bloom cardamom, ginger, mustard seed powder, allspice and thyme 1–2 minutes.
Add carrot, peppers, potato and sweet potato; cover 3–4 minutes until just starting to soften.
Stir in drained black-eyed peas and scotch bonnet; add 2 cups water. Boil.
Cover and simmer 15–20 minutes until vegetables are tender and the stew thickens; mash some beans if liked. Salt; finish with cilantro or parsley.
notes: Tags: Caribbean black eyed peas stew | How to store Caribbean black-eyed peas stew. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Vegan Million Dollar Spaghetti
ingredients: Salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 medium carrot (cut in a ⅕th inch dice)
1 medium bell pepper (any color, cut in a ⅕th inch dice)
1 medium zucchini (cut in a ⅕th inch dice)
1 Italian eggplant (cut in a ⅕th inch dice)
7 oz vegan Italian sausage (approximately two links, crumbled)
28 oz plum tomatoes (place tomatoes in a bowl and break up the whole tomatoes roughly with your fingers)
2 tablespoons fresh oregano (or 2 teaspoons dried oregano)
method: Blend cashews with oregano, parsley, garlic powder, optional nutritional yeast, salt, pepper and 1 cup water to a smooth ricotta.
Soft-fry garlic in oil until fragrant; add onion, pepper and carrot with salt and pepper 2–3 minutes.
Add zucchini and aubergine; cook with optional wine until nearly tender and most moisture is gone.
Stir in tomato paste, crumbled vegan sausage and mince, then plum tomatoes, oregano and 1 cup water. Optional chilli flakes. Simmer low 15 minutes.
Heat oven to 190°C / 375°F. Boil spaghetti al dente; drain. Toss with 1 cup marinara.
Layer half the spaghetti in a pan with half the ricotta, parmesan and mozzarella. Repeat with remaining spaghetti, all remaining sauce and cheeses.
Cover with oiled foil; bake 25 minutes. Uncover 15 minutes more; optional brief broil. Rest 10 minutes.
notes: Tags: vegan million dollar spaghetti recipe. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Besan roti (gluten free roti) recipe
ingredients: ½ to 1 tsp red pepper flakes
½ tsp ground black pepper (optional if using red pepper flakes)
1-2 teaspoons salt (tweak according to your requirements)
method: Boil 1 cup water with turmeric, chilli flakes, cumin, kasoori methi, optional pepper and salt.
On low heat, stir in besan and 1 tbsp oil quickly until a dough forms; mix ~1 minute. Cool 10 minutes.
Knead on an unoiled surface with another tbsp oil until smooth (~1 minute). Rest covered 15–30 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls. On a non-stick surface dusted with besan, roll each to ~18 cm, moving and flouring so it does not stick.
Cook on a hot cast-iron or non-stick griddle; when bubbles form, flip and oil. Roast until spotted golden both sides. Serve at once.
notes: Tags: besan ki roti, besan roti, gluten free roti. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Homemade Crusty Bread
ingredients: 1 teaspoon salt (use less if that's your preference)
Oil or cooking spray for coating bowl and loaf pan
method: Oil a loaf pan or Dutch oven; dust with cornmeal.
Bloom yeast in lukewarm water ~5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in flour and salt to a loose dough.
Oil a bowl; place dough inside, oil the top, and prove warm ~1 hour until more than doubled.
Shape into a loaf (round for a Dutch oven). Place in the pan; dust with flour; proof covered ~45 minutes until domed.
Heat oven to 230°C / 450°F in the last 15 minutes; set a tray of hot water on a lower rack.
Score the loaf; bake middle rack 30 minutes. Cool in the pan 1 hour, then on a rack before slicing.
notes: Tags: crusty bread, crusty bread recipe, Crusty Homemade Bread. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Vegan Coconut Flour Pancakes
ingredients: 2 ½ cups nondairy milk (add 2 cups at first and drizzle in more, a little at a time, if the batter is too thick to form pancakes)
method: Whisk coconut, buckwheat and oat flours with tapioca, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Blend bananas with vinegar, 2 cups plant milk and optional vanilla until smooth.
Whisk puree into dry mix; thin with more milk until pourable. Stir in chia; rest 5–10 minutes.
Cook ⅓-cup rounds on a lightly oiled medium–high griddle until golden underneath; flip and finish. Serve hot.
notes: Tags: Vegan Coconut Flour Pancakes. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Chickpea Tagine Recipe
ingredients: 2 medium carrots (cut into slices or chunks)
14 oz whole plum tomatoes (canned, with juices. Crush the whole tomatoes with your fingers before adding to the pot)
3 cups cooked chickpeas (approximately two 15 oz cans)
2 tablespoons ras el hanout (add more if needed)
¼ tsp saffron (optional. Use the same quantity of turmeric if you don't have saffron)
1 heaping tsp paprika (or cayenne for more heat)
¼ cup cilantro (or parsley, or a mix)
method: Soft-fry sliced onion with ½ tsp salt in olive oil until beginning to caramelise. Cook crushed garlic 1 minute.
Sauté carrots briefly; add raisins.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chickpeas, then ras el hanout, paprika, saffron or turmeric, and herbs.
Add 1 cup water; boil, cover and simmer 30–45 minutes, stirring and adding liquid if needed, until thick.
Fold in olives; adjust salt. Serve.
notes: Tags: chickpea tagine, chickpea tagine recipe, chickpea vegetable tagine, easy chickpea tagine, Moroccan chickpea tagine, spicy chickpea tagine, vegetarian chickpea tagine | Helpful tips and techniques. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Creamy Cauliflower Curry
ingredients: 1 cup full-fat coconut milk (use the thick portion from a can)
1 medium or small head cauliflower (separated into small florets)
1-2 green chili peppers (like serrano or jalapeno. Use less or more depending on your tolerance for heat.)
1 tsp garam masala (optional. Use only if you want a spicier curry. You can also use curry powder instead.)
method: Blend cashews with coconut milk and 1 cup water until silky.
Soft-fry onion and ginger-garlic in 1 tsp coconut oil until translucent (splash of water if sticking). Blend with chilli and ½ cup water smooth.
Simmer the onion paste in remaining oil. Add cauliflower, ½ cup water, cardamom, pepper, chaat masala and kasoori methi.
Cover medium-low 10–15 minutes until tender with a bite (longer if softer preferred).
Stir in cashew-coconut cream; thin if needed. Boil gently; salt and finish with lemon. Serve hot.
notes: Tags: Cauliflower Curry, creamy cauliflower curry, indian cauliflower curry, Malai Gobi. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Creamy Dandelion Soup Recipe
ingredients: 2 loosely packed cups dandelion greens (about 2 ounces)
2 potatoes (boiled, peeled and roughly diced. Use medium-sized russets or larger yellow or red potatoes, about 350 grams total).)
1 tbsp fresh oregano (or 1 tsp dried oregano)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
method: Warm sliced garlic in cold olive oil over medium-low until fragrant and just colouring.
Soft-fry onion and celery until translucent. Wilt dandelion greens a couple of minutes.
Add boiled potatoes and oregano; pour in 2 cups water or stock. Boil; cover and simmer low 5 minutes.
Blend carefully until smooth (vent the lid). Return to the pot; stir in plant milk. Season; warm through. Finish with lemon. Optional swirl of milk to serve.
notes: Tags: dandelion soup, how to cook with dandelion greens. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Vegan Breakfast Casserole
ingredients: 1 tsp avocado oil or any neutral oil
1 tsp fresh rosemary (or sage, If using dried herbs, reduce to 1 tsp)
3 medium potatoes (red or yellow or russet, cut in a ⅓rd inch dice)
3/4 cup raw cashews (soak for 30 minutes unless using a high-powered blender)
Salt and ground black pepper to taste
method: Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F.
Blend cashews with water, onion powder, garlic powder, nutritional yeast, rosemary/sage, salt and pepper until silky.
Boil diced potatoes covered ~10 minutes until very tender; drain.
Soft-fry onion, garlic, parsley and rosemary with salt and pepper ~5 minutes. Add sausage, chilli flakes and potatoes; cook ~5 minutes more. Season.
Spread in an oven-safe skillet or baking dish; pour cheesy sauce evenly over.
Bake 30 minutes until lightly browned; broil ~5 minutes for golden spots. Garnish with parsley; serve hot or room temperature.
notes: Tags: breakfast casserole recipe, cheesy vegan casserole, Vegan Breakfast Casserole, vegan breakfast casserole recipe. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Lebanese chickpea stew recipe
ingredients: 2-3 heaping teaspoons za'atar (add 2 teaspoons first and add more as needed)
1 roasted bell pepper (chopped in small, bite-size pieces)
method: Crush garlic and cumin seeds to a coarse paste.
Sauté paste in olive oil medium-low ~1 minute until fragrant. Cook tomato paste, paprika and chilli flakes a couple of minutes.
Stir in chickpeas, za’atar, roasted pepper and bay leaves.
Add 2 cups water; boil, cover 10 minutes (uncover last 2). Mash some chickpeas to thicken.
Salt; finish with parsley. Serve hot or warm.
notes: Tags: Chickpea Stew, chickpea stew recipe, Lebanese stew, Vegan Chickpea Stew | If you cooked the chickpeas from scratch, you can add the cooking stock back to the stew instead of the 2 cups of water in the recipe. You can also use vegetable stock or vegetable broth instead of water. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Masala Chai Recipe
ingredients: 4 teaspoons sugar (use less or more depending on how sweet you want your chai. See FAQs for sugar-free options)
3 teaspoons loose leaf black tea (use less if you like your tea light)
2 tablespoons vegan creamer (or vegan whipping cream or oat milk or soy milk)
method: Bring water to a boil with chai masala and sugar.
Add tea leaves; boil 1 minute until dark.
Stir in vegan creamer; kill the heat. Cover 3–4 minutes to steep.
Strain into cups; drink hot.
notes: Tags: Masala Chai. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Vaishali (Holy Cow Vegan)

title: Baked BBQ Cauliflower Wings
method: Break cauliflower into florets; rinse.
Whisk flour, salt and paprika with water to a smooth batter. Mix breadcrumbs, panko, flour, paprika and salt for the coating.
Heat oven to 200°C / 400°F. Dip florets in batter then breading; arrange on parchment.
Bake 20–25 minutes until crisp, flipping halfway.
Thin BBQ sauce with water; toss wings to coat. Finish with parsley.
notes: Tags: baked cauliflower wings, bbq cauliflower wings | You can adjust the consistency of the batter by adding more flour if it's too thin and more water if it's too thick. Ideally, it should be between a crepe (thin batter) and a pancake batter (thick batter). Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Elephantastic Vegan

title: Vegan Fish Curry made with Banana Blossoms
ingredients: 2 large pieces banana blossoms in brine (*)
1/2 cup cashew cream (or full-fat coconut milk)
method: Drain and rinse banana blossoms. Marinate ≥20 minutes in water, salt, vinegar, lemon and nori.
Soft-fry onion in oil; add garam masala and ginger 1 minute. Stir in tomato puree and cashew cream; salt and keep warm.
Mix flour, salt and curry powder. Pat blossoms dry; dredge. Grill in a hot oiled pan until marked on all sides.
Reheat curry; plate with blossoms on top. Serve with basmati and naan.
notes: Tags: banana blossom fish curry, vegan fish curry | If your banana blossoms are smaller, you can use these, of course, just make more per serving!. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.
credit: Rewritten for The Starred Kitchen · inspired by Elephantastic Vegan

title: Vegan Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian Spiced Oil) Recipe
ingredients: ½ tsp fenugreek seeds or methi seeds
1 cup extra virgin olive oil (or any neutral oil, including avocado oil, grape seed oil, sunflower oil or safflower oil)
6 cloves garlic (crushed or passed through a garlic press)
method: Lightly crush whole spices (do not powder). Toast in a dry skillet low heat ~5 minutes until aromatic.
Combine toasted spices with oil, onion, garlic and ginger in a small pan.
Bring to a gentle simmer; cook lightly bubbling ~1 hour.
Stir in turmeric (and powdered nutmeg if using) for the last 5 minutes.
Cool completely; strain through cheesecloth or a fine mesh.

title: Berbere (Ethiopian Spice Blend) Recipe
ingredients: ½ tsp fenugreek seeds or methi seeds
6 arbol chili peppers (or any spicy dry red chili peppers)
method: Toast coriander, cardamom, fenugreek, peppercorns, allspice, cloves and cinnamon medium heat 4–5 minutes until fragrant. Off heat, stir in chilli and nutmeg.
Cool; grind with onion flakes to a fine powder.
Stir in paprika, ginger powder and garlic powder.
Store airtight cool and dark, or refrigerate.
notes: Tags: berbere spice blend, Berbere spice mix, ethiopian berbere | The peppercorns and red chili peppers add a good bit of spice to berbere but the spice blend itself is not overwhelmingly spicy. title: Black Bean Hummus Recipe
ingredients: 3 cups canned or cooked black beans (approximately two 14-oz cans)
1 tsp red pepper flakes (use less or more based on your preference)
1 tbsp lemon juice (add more for a tangier hummus)
method: Rinse canned beans if needed; add to a food processor with olives, parsley, garlic, chilli flakes, tahini, lemon and optional za’atar.
Pulse until mostly broken down.
Stream in olive oil while processing until as smooth as liked.
Scoop into a bowl; finish with oil and paprika or za’atar.
notes: Tags: black bean hummus | To make the black bean hummus oil-free add enough vegetable stock or water or the stock from the black beans (if you cooked the black beans from scratch) until you get a smooth texture. title: Crinkle Cut Fries
method: Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F.
Optional peel; wash potatoes. Cut with a crinkle knife into fries.
Pat dry on parchment. Toss with oil and salt until coated; spread in a single layer without overlapping.
Bake ~25 minutes until golden, flipping after 15. Serve with dip; optional parsley.
notes: Tags: crinkle cut chips, crinkle cut fries, wavy fries. Original text rewritten for The Starred Kitchen with attribution.

title: Air Fryer Zucchini
ingredients: 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (skip if oil-free)
method: Slice zucchini ~6 mm thick (thinner cooks faster—under 10 minutes).
Toss with flaxmeal and ½ tsp salt; rest a couple of minutes so moisture helps the flax cling (splash of water if needed).
Coat with chickpea flour, almond flour, cumin, cayenne, optional turmeric, salt and optional oil.
Air-fry at 205°C / 400°F in a single layer 7 minutes; flip; cook 6 minutes more until golden and crusty (~13 minutes total).
Eat at once for maximum crunch; re-crisp briefly in the air fryer if needed.
notes: Tags: Air Fryer Zucchini | Other summer squashes will work just as well in this recipe, including yellow squash and pattypan squash. Make sure you give the zucchini a little time to stand after adding the flaxmeal and salt so it expresses some of its moisture. This will give you the crispiest results.
